summary: The milestone completed 13 experiments in 8.2 minutes, with 8 classified as compute-bound. The 5.23-minute Three-model parser-state and JIT semantic-diversity canary led the recorded compute tail, but the supplied data does not resolve its internal cause, task-time GPU efficiency, or concurrent-model runner behavior.
bottlenecks_identified: The Three-model parser-state and JIT semantic-diversity canary was the longest compute-bound entry, but no phase breakdown is available to locate the cause of its runtime.
Disk-mtime reconstruction ranks elapsed durations but does not provide task-linked stage timing or GPU samples, so the supplied GPU state cannot establish compute-task utilization efficiency.
The data does not establish simultaneous model loading or record runner selection, so it cannot show whether any eligible parallel multi-model task missed DualGPURunner.
improvements_suggested: Emit monotonic per-phase timings for compute-bound experiments, including setup, model loading, inference, and teardown, to localize the longest task's runtime.
Capture GPU utilization and memory samples tagged with the active experiment and phase so end-state idle readings are not mistaken for task-time behavior.
Record concurrent loaded-model count and runner choice, and select DualGPURunner only when at least two models are loaded in parallel.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Add phase-level monotonic timing receipts to every compute-bound experiment.
Join GPU telemetry to experiment and phase identifiers for the full compute interval.
Emit model-concurrency and runner-selection receipts, with conditional DualGPURunner dispatch for parallel multi-model work.
meta_reflection: The reconstructed timings identify where runtime concentrated but not why it concentrated. No measured before-and-after comparison is available, so the retrospective makes no numerical savings claim and prioritizes observability that can support one next milestone.
